title: On stimulated scattering including harmonic generation in an unmagnetized pair plasma for arbitrary pump strengths
abstract: A fully nonlinear analysis for the growth rate of the stimulated backscatter instability of an intense electromagnetic (EM) wave with arbitrary polarization in an unmagnetized pair plasma is presented. The connection of this instability to the FEL process is discussed and utilized. An intense EM wave causes an initially stationary pair plasma to drift forward with a speed near the speed of light. The resulting distribution function for both cold and warm pair plasmas is presented. It is shown that the frequency of the reflected light is thus Doppler downshifted from that of the incident wave. For a linearly polarized EM wave there is also an additional contribution to the forward drift at its second harmonic which leads to backscattered light at all odd harmonics of the Doppler downshifted frequency for sufficiently cold pair plasmas. Fully nonlinear particle-in-cell simulations confirm the theoretical growth rates and show how the instability depends on the pair plasma temperature. The effect of the intensity profile of the incoming EM wave as well as implications for astrophysical pair plasmas is discussed.
